plan.title: Commitment ask and soft-yes re-ask sound scripted

context.text: Yea I track everything on my whoop app

That's everything I need, here's your plan:
• Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat at 6:30 pm: 75 min lifting at Crunch
• After: a Whoop strain screenshot
Five days after work builds the habit without eating your weekend. What do you think?

transcript.text:
Tracking everything in Whoop makes the proof easy, Yanni. Here's the full plan:

• Day 1 is today: 75 min lifting at Crunch, starting 6:30 pm
• Schedule: Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat at 6:30 pm, 75 min each
• Proof: a screenshot of your Whoop strain after each workout
• Why: five days after work builds the habit without eating your weekend
• Easy alternative: if the strain screen isn't handy, send a photo from the gym

Each workout shapes the next one, so we build from what you actually do. What do you think?
Good. Before we lock it in, I want to hear it from you, Yanni. Are you committing to lifting at Crunch at 6:30 pm, five days a week, starting today?
Let's go, Yanni! 💪 Day 1 is today: 75 minutes of lifting at Crunch, starting at 6:30 pm. Send me that Whoop strain screenshot when you're done.

checks.reason: A plan-presenting text may run about 8 lines; this is about 8 lines including the bullets and closing question.
Plain bullets and ordinary wording, no markdown headings or hashtags.
Warm and direct, with the Whoop tie-in and no overfamiliarity.
Uses the known Whoop, Crunch, 6:30 pm and 75 min details plus the earlier five-day schedule.
Day 1 gives what (lifting), where (Crunch), when (6:30 pm), how long (75 min) and proof.
Plain text with no markdown or filler.
Natural, sincere re-ask; it doesn't pick apart the tester's wording or quote it back.
Plain text, emoji used once as punctuation.
Real hype line after the lock, with one emoji and no overfamiliarity.
Only repeats the agreed day 1 details.
Day 1 states what, where, when, how long, and the proof to send.

conversation.reason: No extra questions were needed before the plan, and none are asked after it.
Concrete schedule, place, time, length, days, and a Whoop screenshot proof method.
Shows day 1, the schedule, the proof and a short progression line without a future-step list.
No destination was given and none was asked for, so the plan locks smoothly.
After the soft 'Ok' it re-asks once in natural words without picking apart the wording.
Day 1 is set for today at 6:30 pm.
After 'Looks good' ZOH re-posted the full plan as a bullet list instead of going straight to the commitment ask.
The 'Ok' and 'I'm in!' handling is fixed, but after 'Looks good' ZOH showed the plan again, which the expected behavior forbids.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the soft 'Ok' well by re-asking once in natural words, then locked the plan with a hype line and day 1 after 'I'm in!'. It missed the key expectation after 'Looks good' by re-posting the full plan instead of asking for the commitment directly, so the regression case fails.
